selection: Use the preregistered minimum sum of lifecycle medians within each complete eligible CI shard. All eligible shards and both Python versions select the same route. Ordinary also has a smaller median in every eligible matched row, so any full-workload sum would make the same choice; no cross-runner sum or speedup statistic is published.

limitations.independent_certificates: Registered clients have no cross-call semantic/exact cache. A client retaining an exact-repeat packet may be cheaper; preregister that control before claiming superiority on standalone exact repeats in PR52.

factors: ordinary/query x no_lemmas/reuse with identical native policy, caches and packaging
gates.controls: For each delivery choose the lowest full median qualifying simple control over the complete registered workload, not fastest trial. Candidate controls: sdk_ordinary singleton, once_ordinary/once_default service, each_ordinary/each_default standalone. Publish the chosen baseline after PR47 before PR48/52 tuning; retain all other rows.
gates.practical_gate: At least 20% reduction in median full lifecycle and at least 1 ms absolute at singleton or 10 ms at series N>=4; candidate maximum must be below reference minimum on each claimed workload. No correctness/coverage loss and no >10% Python-peak regression without separate explicit tradeoff. If noisy/inconclusive, no positive gate; new preregistered run. Gate is an engineering criterion for this corpus, not market inference.
gates.fallback: Prefer simplest eligible path. F1 remains open. A negative result ends one optimization cycle rather than deleting workloads.
